issues.description: Plaintext credit card storage - PaymentDetails interface handles raw credit card numbers, CVV, and expiry dates, violating PCI-DSS compliance
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card data. Use a PCI-compliant payment processor like Stripe, PayPal, or Square. Replace PaymentDetails with a payment token/method ID from the processor.

issues.description: Syntax error - incomplete code: 'const paymentSuccessful = await n false;' will crash the application
issues.suggestion: Complete the line: const paymentSuccessful = await chargeCard(payment, amount);

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability - userId parameter lacks validation, and JSON.stringify(features) could be exploited if features array is manipulated
issues.suggestion: Add UUID validation for userId and whitelist validation for feature names. Use parameterized queries with proper input sanitization.

issues.description: Sensitive data logging - console.error may log payment information to application logs, violating PCI-DSS
issues.suggestion: Log only non-sensitive error information (error codes, timestamps). Never log payment details, card info, or full error objects containing sensitive data.

issues.description: Missing authentication and authorization - exported functions don't verify caller authorization, allowing any user to upgrade another user's subscription
issues.suggestion: Add authentication context parameter to verify the caller is authorized to perform operations on the specified userId.

issues.description: Weak card validation - no Luhn algorithm check, accepts any 16-digit string, year parsing assumes 20XX (breaks in 2100), no card type detection
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm for card validation or preferably use a PCI-compliant payment processor that handles validation.

issues.description: Race condition - no transaction management. If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, user is charged without getting subscription
issues.suggestion: Wrap payment and subscription operations in a database transaction to ensure atomicity.

issues.description: No input validation on payment amount - allows negative amounts, extreme values, or NaN. Client-provided amount is trusted instead of server-calculated
issues.suggestion: Validate payment amount is positive, finite, and within reasonable bounds. Never trust client-provided amounts - always calculate server-side.

issues.description: Floating point arithmetic for money - can lead to rounding errors in financial calculations
issues.suggestion: Use integer cents for calculations or implement a Money class. Consider libraries like dinero.js for precise decimal arithmetic.

issues.description: No error recovery or retry logic - transient network/database failures cause payment failures even with valid cards
issues.suggestion: Implement exponential backoff retry logic for transient errors with configurable retry attempts.

issues.description: Hardcoded business logic - pricing, tax rates, fees, and features are hardcoded, requiring code deployment for changes
issues.suggestion: Move configuration to external config file or database for dynamic updates without deployment.

issues.description: Missing rate limiting - no protection against brute-force card attempts or repeated payment requests
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting (e.g., max 3 payment attempts per 15 minutes per user).

issues.description: No idempotency - duplicate requests (network retry, double-click) could charge user twice
issues.suggestion: Add idempotency key parameter to prevent duplicate charges for the same request.

issues.description: Date comparison issue - doesn't account for timezones and uses '<' which may incorrectly deny access on expiration day
issues.suggestion: Use end-of-day for expiration checks and handle timezones properly.

issues.description: Unsafe JSON parsing - JSON.parse() without error handling could crash if database data is corrupted
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch and validate parsed data is an array.

issues.description: Missing type safety - database query results typed as 'any', no type safety for database operations
issues.suggestion: Define TypeScript interfaces for database rows and use typed query methods.

issues.description: Magic numbers - values like 16, 3, 4, 2000 reduce code readability
issues.suggestion: Extract to named constants like CARD_NUMBER_LENGTH, CVV_LENGTH_STANDARD, etc.

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling - some functions throw errors, others return false, making API unpredictable
issues.suggestion: Use consistent error handling strategy with custom error classes for all failure scenarios.

issues.description: No audit logging - critical payment/subscription operations lack audit trail for debugging and compliance
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive logging for all payment and subscription operations with timestamps and user context.

issues.description: Missing input sanitization - card number and CVV not checked for non-numeric characters
issues.suggestion: Sanitize inputs and validate only digits are present in card number and CVV.

issues.description: No unit tests - critical business logic for payment processing lacks any test coverage
issues.suggestion: Implement comprehensive test suite with unit and integration tests targeting 80%+ coverage.

issues.description: Missing JSDoc parameters - comments exist but don't document parameters, return types, or exceptions
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc with @param, @returns, @throws, and @example tags.

issues.description: Missing null/undefined checks - no validation before accessing properties, could throw TypeError if payment object is malformed
issues.suggestion: Add null/undefined checks and type validation before accessing object properties.

issues.description: Consider using enums for tier - string literals could benefit from enum for better type safety
issues.suggestion: Define SubscriptionTier enum with FREE, PREMIUM, ENTERPRISE values.

issues.description: Database connection not managed - import doesn't show connection pooling or management
issues.suggestion: Consider using an ORM like Prisma, TypeORM, or Knex.js for better database management.

codeQuality.summary: This file contains CRITICAL security vulnerabilities that make it unsuitable for production. The code directly handles plaintext credit card data (PCI-DSS violation), has a syntax error on line 48, lacks authentication/authorization, and has zero test coverage for critical payment processing logic. The floating-point arithmetic for money calculations and missing transaction management create significant financial risk.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Main payment flow handles real money transactions with zero validation through tests. Errors could result in financial loss or charging customers incorrectly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful payment processing for both premium and enterprise tiers, invalid card number rejection, insufficient amount rejection, expired card handling, payment gateway failures, and database errors during subscription upgrade.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment gateway integration with no tests. Database insertion failures and network issues are untested.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful card charge, database insertion failures, network timeout scenarios, payment gateway errors, and partial failure recovery with mocked database.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Pricing calculation errors directly impact revenue. Tax and fee calculations use floating-point arithmetic which is error-prone.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier pricing (9.99 + 8% tax + 2.9% fee = 11.08), enterprise tier pricing (49.99 + taxes/fees = 55.44), verify no floating-point rounding errors, test boundary amounts.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Card validation is the first line of defense against invalid payments. Multiple edge cases need testing.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid 16-digit cards, invalid lengths (<16, >16), 3-digit CVV (standard), 4-digit CVV (Amex), invalid CVV lengths, valid/invalid expiry formats (MM/YY), expired cards, cards expiring in current month, future dates, boundary dates (12/99, 01/00).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription upgrades assign features and calculate expiry dates. Incorrect feature assignment or date calculation impacts user experience.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier gets correct 3 features, enterprise gets correct 5 features, subscription expiry is exactly 1 year from now, database upsert for existing subscriptions, JSON feature serialization correctness.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Feature access control determines what premium features users can use. Errors could give free access or block paying customers.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid subscription with feature access grants access, expired subscription denies access, non-existent subscription denies access, invalid feature names return false, JSON parsing errors are handled, subscription at exact expiry boundary.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription retrieval is used throughout the app. Errors in date parsing or JSON deserialization could break functionality.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test existing subscription retrieval returns correct data, non-existent user returns null, date parsing is correct, JSON deserialization works, malformed database data is handled gracefully.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Client-provided amounts could be manipulated. Need to test negative amounts, zero, NaN, Infinity, amounts $0.01 below required.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test payment $0.01 below required amount is rejected, negative amounts throw error, zero amount is rejected, NaN and Infinity are rejected, amount exactly matching required is accepted.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Race conditions in concurrent requests could cause double-charging or inconsistent subscription state.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test two simultaneous payment requests for same user don't cause duplicate charges, database upsert correctly handles concurrent updates, transaction isolation prevents race conditions.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: Zero test coverage for business-critical payment processing logic. No test files exist for this 190-line file containing financial transactions, card validation, pricing calculations, and subscription management. This represents severe risk for production deployment.

suggestions.description: Apply Repository Pattern to separate data access from business logic
suggestions.before: Direct database queries scattered throughout: await db.query(query, [userId, tier, validUntil, JSON.stringify(features)])
suggestions.after: Create SubscriptionRepository and PaymentRepository classes with methods like create(), findByUserId(), recordPayment() that encapsulate all database operations
suggestions.benefits: Separates data access concerns, makes code testable with dependency injection, centralizes queries for easier maintenance, follows Single Responsibility Principle

suggestions.description: Apply Strategy Pattern for payment gateway abstraction
suggestions.before: Direct payment processing in chargeCard() function with hardcoded logic
suggestions.after: Create PaymentGateway interface with charge() method, implement StripePaymentGateway, PayPalGateway, etc. allowing easy switching between providers
suggestions.benefits: Enables multiple payment providers, better error handling with typed results, improved testability through interface abstraction, follows Open/Closed Principle

suggestions.description: Extract Value Objects for CardNumber, CVV, and ExpiryDate with built-in validation
suggestions.before: validatePaymentDetails() function with manual string checks
suggestions.after: Create CardNumber.create(), CVV.create(), ExpiryDate.create() that throw domain exceptions on invalid input, making invalid states unrepresentable
suggestions.benefits: Encapsulates validation within domain objects, fail-fast with immediate validation, type safety ensures valid data throughout application, eliminates separate validation function

suggestions.before: Hardcoded pricing, tax rates, and fees in calculateSubscriptionPrice() function
suggestions.after: Create PricingService class with configurable PricingConfig, use Money value object to handle cents, add methods calculateTax() and calculateProcessingFee()
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes pricing configuration, eliminates floating-point precision issues with Money class, makes pricing testable and configurable per environment, explicit calculation methods

suggestions.description: Create SubscriptionService class to centralize business logic following domain-driven design
suggestions.before: Procedural processPremiumPayment() function with mixed concerns
suggestions.after: SubscriptionService with upgradeToPremium(), hasFeatureAccess(), getActiveSubscription() methods, constructor-injected dependencies (repositories, payment gateway, pricing service)
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes business logic, clear dependency injection for testability, better error handling with custom exceptions, follows Single Responsibility Principle

suggestions.description: Use TypeScript enums and const assertions for better type safety
suggestions.before: String literal types: tier: 'free' | 'premium' | 'enterprise', features: string[]
suggestions.after: Create SubscriptionTier enum, SUBSCRIPTION_FEATURES const object with as const, use ReadonlyArray for immutability
suggestions.benefits: Compile-time type safety, autocomplete support, prevents typos in feature strings, better IDE support and refactoring

suggestions.description: Create domain-specific exception classes instead of generic Error
suggestions.after: Create PaymentError, InvalidCardNumberError, InvalidCVVError, ExpiredCardError, InsufficientPaymentError, PaymentFailedError exception hierarchy
suggestions.benefits: More specific error handling, better error tracking and logging, enables catching specific error types, clearer intent and debugging

suggestions.description: Extract magic numbers into named constants
suggestions.after: Create PAYMENT_CONSTANTS object with CARD_NUMBER_LENGTH: 16, CVV_LENGTH_STANDARD: 3, CVV_LENGTH_AMEX: 4, SUBSCRIPTION_DURATION_YEARS: 1
suggestions.benefits: Self-documenting code, single source of truth, easy to modify values, improved readability

suggestions.description: Replace boolean returns with Result discriminated union types
suggestions.before: Promise<boolean> return types lose error information
suggestions.after: Use Result<T, E> type: { success: true; value: T } | { success: false; error: E } for richer error details
suggestions.benefits: No silent failures, forces explicit error handling, type-safe error information, better debugging with detailed context

suggestions.description: Add Logger injection for better observability
suggestions.before: console.error('Payment failed:', error) directly in code
suggestions.after: Create Logger interface with info(), warn(), error(), debug() methods, inject ConsoleLogger or Winston/Pino implementation
suggestions.benefits: Testable logging (can mock in tests), consistent log format, easy to swap implementations, structured logging with context, better production observability

refactorings.summary: The code needs significant architectural refactoring to separate concerns, improve testability, and follow SOLID principles. Key improvements include implementing Repository pattern for database access, Strategy pattern for payment processing, extracting Value Objects for validation, creating a dedicated SubscriptionService, and modernizing TypeScript usage with enums and proper error handling.

recommendations.description: IMMEDIATE: Remove all plaintext credit card handling and integrate PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal, Square). Current implementation violates PCI-DSS and exposes application to severe legal and financial risks.
IMMEDIATE: Fix syntax error on line 48 ('const paymentSuccessful = await n false;'). This will crash the application and prevent deployment.
URGENT: Implement comprehensive test suite for payment processing logic. Current 0% coverage on financial transactions is unacceptable for production. Target 80%+ coverage before deployment.
URGENT: Implement database transaction management to wrap payment charging and subscription upgrade in atomic operations. Current race condition risks charging users without granting subscriptions.
Add authentication and authorization checks to all exported functions. Users should only be able to modify their own subscriptions.
Implement input validation for all user-provided data including userId (UUID format), payment amounts (positive, finite, reasonable bounds), and feature names (whitelist).
Remove sensitive data from error logs. Replace console.error with structured logging that excludes payment details, card information, and sensitive user data.
Refactor to Repository pattern and Service layer architecture. Extract SubscriptionRepository, PaymentRepository, and SubscriptionService to separate data access from business logic.
Replace floating-point money calculations with integer cents or use a decimal library (dinero.js) to avoid rounding errors in financial transactions.
Implement rate limiting on payment processing endpoints (e.g., max 3 attempts per 15 minutes per user) to prevent brute-force attacks and abuse.
Add idempotency key support to prevent duplicate charges from network retries or user double-clicks. Store and check idempotency keys before processing payments.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient database and network failures during payment processing.
Extract hardcoded business logic (pricing, tax rates, fees, features) to configuration files or database for dynamic updates without code deployment.
Add comprehensive JSDoc documentation with @param, @returns, @throws, and @example tags for all public functions.
Modernize TypeScript usage with enums for SubscriptionTier, const assertions for features, readonly modifiers, and typed database query results.
